snippets.text: Normal liver volume in adults ranges from 1000-1500 ml (approximately 20-25 ml/kg body weight). Hepatomegaly is defined as liver volume >1500 ml or >2 SD above mean for body surface area.

Hepatic resectability requires: future liver remnant (FLR) ≥20% in normal liver, ≥30% in chemotherapy-treated liver, ≥40% in cirrhotic liver. Tumor-to-liver ratio >30% is associated with inadequate FLR.

Couinaud segments guide anatomical liver resection. Right hepatectomy removes segments V-VIII. Left hepatectomy removes segments II-IV. Segment I (caudate) is considered separately. Portal vein branches define segment boundaries.

LI-RADS v2018 categorizes hepatocellular carcinoma risk: LR-1 (definitely benign), LR-2 (probably benign), LR-3 (intermediate), LR-4 (probably HCC), LR-5 (definitely HCC ≥10mm with major HCC features). Arterial phase hyperenhancement and washout are major features.

Fleischner Society guidelines for incidental lung nodules (2017): Solid nodule <6mm: no routine follow-up (low risk). 6-8mm: 6-12 month CT follow-up. >8mm: consider PET-CT or biopsy. Ground-glass nodules require longer follow-up intervals (24 months for persistent GGO >6mm).

TNM 8th edition lung staging: T1 ≤3cm, T2 3-5cm, T3 5-7cm, T4 >7cm or invasion. N0 no nodes, N1 ipsilateral hilar, N2 ipsilateral mediastinal, N3 contralateral. M0 no metastasis, M1a contralateral lung/pleural, M1b single extrathoracic, M1c multiple extrathoracic.
